Thanks to a sluggish economic recovery from the Great Recession and backlash against the passage of the Affordable Care Act, Republicans took control of the House with a 63-seat gain – the largest House sweep since the 1940s – and won six seats in the Senate. Former state lawmaker Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins defeated three Republicans, including one endorsed by President Donald Trump. His victory means Democrats will control the governor's office in 30 states, including several they flipped after years of Republican control in places such as Iowa, Georgia, Ohio and Texas.
